sources.title: Circulating follicular helper T cells are increased in systemic sclerosis and promote plasmablast differentiation through the IL-21 pathway which can be inhibited by ruxolitinib
studyModel: human SSc cohort: 50 patients and 32 controls

sources.title: T follicular helper-like cells contribute to skin fibrosis
Imbalance toward TFH 1 cells playing a role in aberrant B cell differentiation in systemic sclerosis
studyModel: human circulating Tfh subset case-control analysis

claims.limitation: Increased cTfh cell numbers in one cohort; do not generalise to all cohorts or conflate absolute counts with proportions.
IL-21R blockade and ruxolitinib effects in coculture are not clinical efficacy evidence.
Correlation of ICOS+ Tfh-like infiltration with dermal fibrosis does not establish human causality.
Anti-ICOS and IL-21 neutralisation effects apply to the reported GVHD-SSc mouse model; no human treatment conclusion.
Overall cTfh proportion unchanged while Tfh1 frequency increased; subset changes must not be misreported as total cTfh increase.

disagreements.description: Ricard et al. report increased circulating Tfh cell numbers, while Ly et al. report no difference in overall cTfh proportion but an increased Tfh1 subset.
requiresReview: CXCR5/PD-1 gating and Tfh1 subset definitions
disagreements.interpretation: Potentially compatible measurements; do not classify as a confirmed biological contradiction.
